status_summary: The administration moved to end Flores through the courts: the Justice Department moved to terminate the settlement on 2025-05-22, Chief Judge Dolly M. Gee denied the motion on 2025-08-15, and the government appealed; the Ninth Circuit heard argument on 2026-06-02 (No. 25-6308) and no decision was found. No statute repealing or amending TVPRA section 235, setting national detention standards or moving custody of unaccompanied children from HHS to DHS was found, and the Office of Refugee Resettlement still runs the program. HHS proposed a rule on 2026-06-26 that would tighten sponsor identity, income and background checks for released children, with comments due 2026-08-25.

timeline.event: The Justice Department moved in the Central District of California to terminate the Flores Settlement Agreement.
Chief Judge Dolly M. Gee denied the motion to terminate the Flores Settlement Agreement and dissolve the 2019 injunction, finding no changed circumstances or other ground for relief under Rule 60(b).
The Ninth Circuit heard the government's appeal of the denial (Flores v. Blanche, No. 25-6308); press reports said the panel questioned the case for ending the decree.

HHS's Office of Refugee Resettlement proposed a rule requiring specified identity documents, proof of income and wider background checks for sponsors of unaccompanied children (comments to 2026-08-25).

title: Repeal TVPRA section 235, end the Flores agreement, move child custody from HHS to DHS
uncertainties: The filing date of the motion comes from a tracking site and was not checked against the docket. The Ninth Circuit argument is confirmed by the court's calendar and a Bloomberg Government report; plaintiffs' counsel's case page lists briefing from December 2025 to February 2026 and no decision, and a search in this review found none. The same page reports that the district court appointed a special master and independent monitor on 2026-08-18 for certain CBP and ICE facilities; it is an advocacy source and the order was not read, so it is not used. Bills introduced in December 2025 (H.R. 6389 and S. 3322) would loosen fees and information sharing for unaccompanied children in the opposite direction and neither addresses TVPRA, Flores or custody. No administration bill on this topic and no DHS rule on alien minors was found in a Federal Register search. HHS sponsor-rule changes are a related ORR vetting step, not custody transfer. Litigation over Flores as a DOJ priority is also covered in c17-06.
